audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 2 and 3 were given to Volibear and 2+ items to Skill; the applied mirror sets Levels 2 and 3 to Skill and 2+ items to Volibear.
audit.why: Dredge Line reaches 1150 and Thundering Smash charges 300, so the early walk-up is contested, not free; and a full-tank Nautilus at two items has no damage to kill a drain-tank, so the late duel is Volibear's.
audit.corrected: phases[1].side/win[1] and phases[2].side/win[2] to Skill, phases[6].side/win[6] to Volibear; ratings 5, 5 and 7.

audit.why: Spike windows (3-5, level 6 Stormbringer, first item, late) are right; only their captions needed the real cooldowns and the corrected late-game owner.
audit.corrected: spikes[0] now names Dredge Line's 14s rank-1 timer and Titan's Wrath's 12s shield; spikes[3] now says the 1v1 stays yours and names the CC chain as the actual danger.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two real errors. (1) 'Titan's Wrath passive stun' — Titan's Wrath is the W shield; the passive is Staggering Blow, and it ROOTS, it does not stun. (2) 'W shred' for Frenzied Maul — W applies on-hit and marks; the second cast into the mark is what heals Volibear.
audit.why: A player who thinks the shield stuns will hold his Q for a CC that never comes from that source, and one who thinks W shreds will not bother re-casting into the mark — losing the heal that carries the whole extended trade.
audit.corrected: Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against a target. Titan's Wrath is a 12s shield that adds damage-over-time to his attacks. Riptide slows on 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s. Frenzied Maul (5s) marks and applies on-hit; the re-cast into the mark deals bonus damage and heals.

edits.before: Q + W online — stun in, double-bite out. Nautilus has to respect every walk-up once your second W heal-bite threatens.
edits.after: Q + W online, but a 1150-range Dredge Line beats a 300-unit charge — bait the hook into a minion before you step up.

edits.before: Level 2 you keep the trading edge with sustained basic damage he can't match.
edits.after: Level 2 is even — Dredge Line hooks from 1150 range and drags you back.

edits.before: E completes the pattern: shield yourself as you disengage or slow Nautilus under the sky-splitter. This is the start of your kill window.
edits.after: Sky Splitter slows and shields you if you stand in the blast, but Riptide is back every 6s at rank 3 — trade, then leave before it lands.

edits.before: At level 3 your Q stun and W shred hard-outtrade his defensive kit.
edits.after: Level 3 is even: Riptide's 6s slow keeps peeling your walk-up.

edits.before: With two-plus items Nautilus becomes an unkillable CC tank and his scaling wins.
edits.after: At 2+ items the duel is yours — his tank build has no damage to kill you.

edits.before: You out-DPS Nautilus in every extended trade. Bait his Q Dredge Line into a minion or sidestep it, then walk him down with Q Thundering Smash stun and W Frenzied Maul. His Titan's Wrath shield and Riptide are defensive — they don't out-trade your sustained damage.
edits.after: You out-DPS Nautilus in extended trades, but only once his tools are spent: bait Dredge Line (14s at rank 1) into a minion, wait out Riptide's slow, then Q Thundering Smash in and cash both Frenzied Maul bites. Titan's Wrath shields him for 12s — bite through it, don't burst into it.

edits.before: Nautilus scales into a near-unkillable tank/support with permanent CC. His Riptide, Titan's Wrath, and Depth Charge lock you down long enough for his team to collapse, and you can't kill him fast enough anymore.
edits.after: Nautilus scales into a tank with no kill pressure of his own, so the 1v1 stays yours. The danger is the chain: Staggering Blow roots on his first hit, Riptide slows every 5s, Depth Charge knocks up — never fight him beside his team.

edits.before: With two-plus items Nautilus flips into a problem. As a full tank he becomes nearly unkillable, and his Riptide slow, Titan's Wrath passive stun, and point-and-click Depth Charge chain enough CC to hold you still while his team kills you. Your damage no longer outpaces his bulk, so your lead has to already be won.
edits.after: With two-plus items the duel is yours: a full-tank Nautilus carries no damage to finish you, and Frenzied Maul's 5s re-bite out-heals his chip. What still hurts is the CC chain — Staggering Blow roots on his first hit, Riptide slows every 5s, Depth Charge knocks you up — so take him where his team cannot collapse on the lock-up.

edits.before: Use Q stun and W shred to win every extended trade
edits.after: Q stun in, then re-bite the Frenzied Maul mark

edits.before: You spike levels 3-6 hard — that's the kill window. See the level-by-level chart for the swing points.
edits.after: Your window runs levels 4-6 and again at two items. See the level-by-level chart for the swing points.

notes: Both packet suspectNames ('His Titan's Wrath', 'His Depth Charge') are FALSE POSITIVES — both are real Nautilus ability names; the near-miss is only the leading pronoun. The genuine error on this page was calling Titan's Wrath a stun: the root belongs to the passive, Staggering Blow. Chart rows 2, 3 and 2+ items flipped as one paired group to match the applied mirror.
